sections.title: Root Shape
sections.question: What should a user see first when they run the AEAT CLI?

decision.note: Looks good. I like the fact that there is a clear separation between the actual setup and the app interface. Good

Check is not accepted because it's ambiguous. What I think you might mean is status.

Start is also not something CLI uses, and I firmly rejected it. Setup, init, setup, create, and so forth are CLI keywords and verbs. Start isn't. It's also ambiguous and uncertain what we are starting.

Can you confirm explicitly that it will begin a complete flow of setup initiation processes and an application that will be responsible for setting up all authentication interface and every single aspect of checking, verification, and scaffolding, including token ingestion? Persistence profile setup and so forth? Is that what you are thinking of adding to setup? If that's the case we have to make sure we have content for this

sections.title: App Recovery
sections.question: Should the app have status and next-action commands?

decision.note:
Status: I don't think it's possible for the whole application to say "status." If I don't know, I reject "status." It's wrong.
- There is no place for it.
- It is completely ambiguous and completely wrong.
- There is nothing it refers to.
- The application is a container, and the actual applications (the mini CLIs and APIs) contained within the app domain have no next semantic understanding.
It is completely wrong

sections.title: Evidence Domain Name
sections.question: What should we call the domain for statements, invoices, receipts, and transactions?

decision.note:
I like Ledger because that's what financial transaction container databases are usually called. The issue is that, while incoming financial transactions will be under it, invoices we issue or receive might not be covered by this. It's worth thinking about a better solution.

I do not like Records, Movements, or Evidence. None of them relate to what this section should be about: the ingestion of external incoming financial data

sections.title: Import Grammar
sections.question: Should imports be workflow-first or resource-first?

decision.note: Resource-first all the way, absolutely better, easier to understand and clearer. I'm concerned that you are mixing plural and singular forms of nouns. Just a note to make sure that these are standardised. It's a UX usability issue if the user cannot anticipate plural or singular forms of nouns.

sections.title: Transaction Work
sections.question: What language should transaction cleanup use?

decision.note:
Difficult for me to make a decision because I do not have the ability to understand what prepare means. Split is clear but I do not understand what MOV or TX lines refer to. This needs proper design as a mini application on its own to provide a clear, well-structured README so that the user understands. Worth another review pass.

I'm also extremely concerned about clean, which means that transactions would be deleted wholesale. Data safety is paramount because the data needs to be persisted at all costs and treated not as transient but as legally binding and mission-critically important. No command should ever, under any circumstance, delete or remove data without very strict user supervision and authorisation from the data persistence policy guardrail

sections.title: Invoices And Receipts
sections.question: What invoice and receipt states must the CLI expose?

decision.note:
We are conflating invoices and receipts. I think there is a very important distinction between the tax system and the CLI's misunderstanding of the actual purchase invoices related to the ledger.

I think this whole issue needs to be audited. Ledger is incoming transactions that deal with sanitization and metadata assignment, and that includes invoice treatment because purchases have invoices and receipts. They are the same thing. However I'm concerned that what you are conflating is invoices issued to third-party tax entities or invoices from third-party tax entities related to business operations. These are completely unrelated concepts within the tax systems in general and in the Spanish tax system.

I cannot even provide preliminary feedback on this until this has been rigorously separated and clarified. Generally speaking it feels like we are conflating domains and we are not respecting the text operations, transaction incoming data operations, and text filing operations

sections.title: Declarations Domain
sections.question: Should the tax-output domain be declarations?

decision.note: The noun declarations: I do not necessarily love it but I do not reject it. Can you please find me alternatives so that I can maybe consider more user-friendly options that are clearer about what this CLI application entry point is all about? It could be Modelo, could be filing, could be declaration, and so forth

sections.title: Finding What To File
sections.question: Should users run obligations find, or should declaration finding be simpler?

decision.note: I don't quite see obligations. I think there is again some sort of application misunderstanding because obligations is a property of the setup process. A profile will be required to enrol in a tax regimen. In other words an active profile will have obligations already assigned. Feels out of place but perhaps a misunderstanding. Please audit. This is not quite ready yet

sections.title: Declaration Grammar
sections.question: Should declarations be batch-first or modelo-first?

decision.note:
I am concerned about the commands prepare, review, and validate. Only validate and export seem like understandable commands. Prepare and review are completely ambiguous and I do not see any calculation commands. This feels like a hollow shell of a text processing command structure and CLI application.

This needs rigorous multi-turn and wave auditing to ensure that the CLI is actually capable of calculating the contents of period-spanning cross-referenced and live-review-backed modelo calculations. This feels too premature to give you any sort of guided or preliminary review. Needs more work

sections.title: Periods And Deadlines
sections.question: How should the CLI handle forgotten periods and deadlines?

decision.note:
History is ambiguous. I think there are better words. Archive will be one of them. I'm having real difficulty with periods.

I think what you are trying to do is declare an Overview command that deals with calendar events in Roman status and, within the obligation framework, defines and gets, based on remote authenticated A/E/A/D available data, the status of the filing history and any sort of declaration that might be in-flight (work in progress, etc.). This probably needs a complete UX redesign.

I'm wondering whether a calendar-oriented representation that outlines the enrolled, authenticated enrollment tax system and modello obligations versus the known in-flight modello pipeline ingestion and so forth status properties as a cohesive command might be the better option to proceed with

sections.title: Corrections
sections.question: How should after-deadline or revised calculations work?

decision.note:
It feels like corrections are exactly the same as a standard filing. I believe the Spanish text system deals with follow-up filings in exactly the same technical manner as normal filings, except there are property values to indicate they are follow-up. They probably require a reference CSV number or some other identity notification to link against the original filing.

I would advise against introducing corrections in this line. Instead consider adding corrections as a feature flag that requires a CSV or ID number to link against an already filed return. Internal application constraints and library capabilities must be able to handle correction filing, checking whether the CSV filing is actually correct and refiling as a correction the correct form. The form is compatible and amendable and so forth. This needs complete research against the capabilities and rulesets of the AEAT websites

sections.title: Blocked Report
sections.question: Should blocked-report be a standalone output?

decision.note:
I have no idea what Blocked Report means. This feels extremely flimsy. It needs more work. Export is understandable but the most important aspect is that the format is missing.

We do want to export a PDF using a preview template that AEAT might be able to provide. The backend needs to be implemented so that we are actually able to hook up to the remote AEAT system, provide calculation data, feed it, and get a preview filing PDF.

We also want to support JSON, TOML, CSV, and other formats and syntax that the internal AEAT system supports for data and model or calculation import when manually filing the actual forms. Check please!

This is not something I anticipated, but I like the feature and keep it. It's difficult to understand exactly what audit means. Evidence and records are clearer, but I am extremely concerned we are conflating again internal ledger information versus other calculation, evidence, and documentation.

The feature that you seem to be describing is somehow accounting metadata exposure as separate commands, but I am concerned that this does not warrant to be exported into full commands. I think every transaction that is considered a business transaction and is part of a tax filing has evidence by rule. Basically, any transaction that has no evidence, such as an invoice or receipt, or an invoice that we got or sent to third-party tax entities without actual PDF or some sort of programmatic data that certifies the actual invoice, cannot exist in a tax declaration system without records and evidence. So this whole section feels tautological and nonsensical. Needs reviewing because I'm not sure what you want to achieve

sections.title: Workspaces
sections.question: Should save/load be the recovery model?

decision.note:
OK I like the idea of workspaces but I don't know what you mean by it so I cannot give you any feedback.

What worries me is that you're conflating text profiles, which would be the workspace as I understand it in a normal application context. This needs reviewing. Workspace is something that I do not want to put in explicitly. If you mean "set up a profile," which we would handle not in the application domain, then okay, review

sections.title: Output And Safety
sections.question: Which output and safety gates are mandatory?

decision.note:
Can I say that I think the profile-based way of working is not correct?
If you look at G client, the whole system mandates an active authentication profile and assumes that any command run in the application is against the authentication profile we set up in setup. I would drop profile.
Workspace is ambiguous, as I have told you already. It does not feel like a catch-all but dry run does.
The only two things that I would mandate for all commands are:
- dry run
- help (which is missing)
Drop the specific profile in workspace commands and make it conditional on the actual written findings of audit. Also revise the output because I have requested support for TOML, JSON, CSV, and other AE/AT-compatible formats for export, including PDF. This definitely needs a lot more thought

sections.title: ADR Readiness
sections.question: What is the correct status after this approval session?

decision.note: None of the options (revise, keep, or reject) is appropriate. This is in-flight and we're going to be chiselling and working based on repeated flows of this whole approval CLI session. Keep the ADR open and marked as in progress please
